summary.oneLiner: FY26 revenue flat YoY due to a temporary ~30% US export hit from tariffs, but margins expanded on mix shift to machined components and strong Europe/India growth; with US duties now at 25% and RoR fully settled, FY27 guides to mid-teen growth as US orders resume and European programs ramp.

one-line thesis: FY26 revenue flat YoY due to a temporary ~30% US export hit from tariffs, but margins expanded on mix shift to machined components and strong Europe/India growth; with US duties now at 25% and RoR fully settled, FY27 guides to mid-teen growth as US orders resume and European programs ramp.
financial scorecard: Revenue FY26: INR1,144 cr (flat YoY vs ~INR1,143 cr implied); Gross margin: 49.4%→51.5%; EBITDA margin: >20% maintained; PAT: not explicitly stated in transcript; One-offs: INR22 cr US customs duty expense (partially recoverable from customers, revenue recognition lagged to Q1–Q2 FY27) and INR6 cr legal/professional fees for RoR settlement; Order book: 3–6 month visible, ~INR115–125 cr/month dispatches planned for H1 FY27; Net debt: effectively zero post full RoR payment of INR101 cr on 31-Mar-2026; cash surplus ~INR367 cr.
guidance: Revenue growth: FY27 mid-teen (15–17%), FY28 high-teen or higher; Margins: normalized EBITDA 20.5–21%+, gross margin 49–53% range; Order inflow: US recovery from Q1 FY27, Europe programs ramping to 50–60% of peak in FY27; Capex/commissioning: ~INR30–40 cr/year (maintenance + selective expansions), no major greenfield announced.
order book & pipeline: Program awards typically 5–7 years; near-term visibility 3–6 months; H1 FY27 planned monthly dispatches INR115–125 cr; new European plant programs starting at 10–20% and ramping through FY27; some US programs previously on hold now re-engaging.
segment / subsidiary detail: FY26 split (INR cr): Domestic bearing rings 386; Domestic auto components 170; Export bearing rings 154; Export auto components 350; Scrap 71; Export incentives 13; Total ~1,143. FY25 split (INR cr): Domestic bearing rings 329; Domestic auto components 177; Export bearing rings 155; Export auto components 399; Scrap 78; Export incentives 16. Auto components now ~50%+ of revenue; ~85% of component revenue is machined vs 15% forged-only.
growth verticals / optionality: Europe China+1 wins (60% of new nominations from Europe in FY26); US recovery as tariffs normalize; domestic import substitution in larger bearing rings; early EV/industrial programs; potential new customer programs converting after 15–18 month validation (impact from FY28).
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin expansion driven by higher-value machined mix and steel sourcing shifts (more domestic); quarterly raw-material pass-through for most overseas customers (some half-yearly); freight/container constraints causing 2–3 week delays and premium costs but manageable via consignment/warehouse inventory.
capex / expansion: ~INR30–40 cr/year anticipated (maintenance + targeted capacity for high-utilization product ranges); FY26 actual capex ~INR36 cr; cold/warm forging not immediate, focused on maximizing hot forging assets.
capital allocation: INR101 cr RoR settlement completed (balance sheet clean, no covenants); Board approved buyback of 1 cr shares at INR180/share (INR180 cr), promoters not participating; open to further dividends but retaining cash for uncertainty and selective capex.
risks & watch-items: US tariff policy volatility (Section 232 at 25% remains); container/freight cost inflation and transit delays; customer inventory rebuild pace; geopolitical disruptions; EV transition timing (currently limited traction vs ICE/hybrid).
management quality / tone: Confident and pragmatic; emphasizes resilience, relationship depth, and balance sheet strength; conservative on recognizing recoverable duty revenues; constructive on FY27 recovery and multi-year ramp.
non-obvious takeaways: INR22 cr customs duty expense booked conservatively in Q4 with corresponding revenue delayed to Q1–Q2 FY27 as customers lift consignment stock; partial refund expected from US government for pre-Nov-2025 IEEPA-related excess duties, which would flow to revenue when received; utilization ~62–63% overall but some product lines at 80–85%, driving targeted capex needs.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.
